# Aura3D (full agent guide)

> Aura3D | Build playable 3D worlds in TypeScript — typed scenes, looks, typed GLB/glTF assets, camera rigs, gameFeel, and gameplay through `@aura3d/engine` plus the `@aura3d/cli` toolchain, for browser 3D apps and interactive websites. Start with https://aura3d.auraone.ai/llms.txt (fast path); this file is the long form.

Play browser games made with Aura3D, explore the TypeScript behind their worlds, and start your own game or product viewer from a working project.

## Facts

- Product: AI-native TypeScript 3D SDK for browser 3D apps, interactive websites, and prompt-to-code scene kits
- Website: https://aura3d.auraone.ai
- Current release: Aura3D 5.7.1 (per the repo manifest — the same source the build's version guard uses)
- Docs: https://aura3d.auraone.ai/docs/api
- Showcase gallery: https://aura3d.auraone.ai/apps/showcase-index/ (30 playable games; add `?autoplay=1` to any game URL and the computer plays it)
- Sitemap: https://aura3d.auraone.ai/sitemap.xml
- Crawl policy: https://aura3d.auraone.ai/robots.txt (public content allow-all; build internals and source maps disallowed)
- Last updated: 2026-11-19

## Pages

- [Home](https://aura3d.auraone.ai/): Play browser games made with Aura3D, explore the TypeScript behind their worlds, and start your own game or product viewer from a working project.

### Docs

- [Quickstart: Build a 3D product viewer with Aura3D](https://aura3d.auraone.ai/docs/agent-quickstart): Create a product viewer with a model, studio lighting, and an orbit camera. Everything you need for the first frame comes with the starter.
- [Configure an AI coding agent for Aura3D](https://aura3d.auraone.ai/docs/agent-rules): Point your coding assistant to the public API, the asset manifest, and the starter source before asking it to edit a scene.
- [Aura3D TypeScript scene API](https://aura3d.auraone.ai/docs/api): Import the scene, camera, materials, and interactions you need. The engine mounts them together and owns the frame loop.
- [Import and validate a 3D model with Aura3D](https://aura3d.auraone.ai/docs/assets): Register a GLB or glTF file once. The CLI records its source and generates a TypeScript name you can use in your scene.
- [Aura3D vs. Three.js: a complete engine vs a rendering library](https://aura3d.auraone.ai/docs/aura3d-vs-threejs): Aura3D ships the renderer, typed assets, AI generation, game kit and deploy checks that three.js leaves to you. A lit, framed product in 10 lines against 38.
- [Aura3D capabilities and proof](https://aura3d.auraone.ai/docs/claims): What Aura3D 5.7.1 ships: the typed browser 3D workflow, the renderer, the asset pipeline and AI generation, the game stack, and the proof behind each.
- [Build an Aura3D scene with Claude](https://aura3d.auraone.ai/docs/claude): Give Claude the project context, a working starter, and one visible change to make. Review the result in the browser.
- [Use Cursor with an Aura3D project](https://aura3d.auraone.ai/docs/cursor): Open the scaffolded project in Cursor. Follow a typed asset from its manifest to the scene, then make one change you can see.
- [Deploy an Aura3D app to a static host](https://aura3d.auraone.ai/docs/deployment): Build your static files, validate the asset manifest, and check the distribution folder before uploading it to your host.
- [Verify an Aura3D scene and its assets](https://aura3d.auraone.ai/docs/evidence): Trace a capability from the working example to its source, asset record, or deployment check.
- [Aura3D developer documentation](https://aura3d.auraone.ai/docs/): Start with a working TypeScript scene. Learn to frame a model, light its surfaces, or build a game around a playable starter.
- [Migrate from Aura3D 4.x to 5.0.1](https://aura3d.auraone.ai/docs/migration/4-to-5): Upgrade guide from Aura3D 4.x to 5.0.1: who is affected, upgrade steps, breaking changes, behavior changes, new opt-in features and removed deprecated APIs.
- [Write prompts for Aura3D scenes](https://aura3d.auraone.ai/docs/prompt-recipes): Start with a subject, camera, and interaction. Match the brief to a scene kit, then change the resulting TypeScript.
- [Choose an Aura3D starter template](https://aura3d.auraone.ai/docs/templates): Choose a viewer for a product shot, a cinematic scene for a camera study, or a game for movement, scoring, and input. Each starter gives you the TypeScript source.

<!-- agent-guide: everything below this marker is the long-form agent guide; gen-seo.mjs preserves it verbatim -->
Aura3D agent guide — a typed scene API for building real 3D apps: scenes, looks,
lighting, materials, typed assets, camera rigs, gameFeel, SDF text, decals, rigid bodies, and gameplay through
`@aura3d/engine` plus the `@aura3d/cli` toolchain. Current release: see Facts above. It includes the game kit, QA replay hooks, safety net, audio synth, model loader, GLSL chunks, scatter/merge helpers, racket-sports kits and CLI asset tools.

three.js to Aura3D: if you would write the left column, write the middle one. Every Aura3D line is type-checked in docs/agents/recipes-src/translation-table.check.ts.

Aura3D is a complete engine with its own renderer: you describe a scene as typed nodes and `createAuraApp` owns the renderer, camera aspect, resize, loop, context loss and disposal. Delete that plumbing instead of porting it. Every Aura3D line below is type-checked against the engine in `recipes-src/translation-table.check.ts` (recipes-src/translation-table.check.ts) (`pnpm exec tsc -p docs/agents/recipes-src/tsconfig.json`). Complete scenes with no admitted models: `recipes.md` (recipes.md) recipes 8 to 15.

| If you would write (three.js) | Write (Aura3D) | Difference that bites |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Scene` + `PerspectiveCamera` + `WebGLRenderer` + `setAnimationLoop` | `scene({ background }).camera(camera.perspective({ position, target, fov }))` then `createAuraApp("#app", { scene })`; per frame `app.onFrame((f) => ...)` with `f.dt`; `app.ready().then(...)` (never a top-level `await`) | No renderer, resize or loop code. Mount target is a `<canvas>` or a sized wrapper. |
| `new Mesh(geometry, material)` | `primitives.box({ name, size: [w, h, d], material: material.pbr({ color }) })` (also `sphere`, `plane`, `cylinder`, `capsule`, `cone`, `torus`, `torusKnot`, `lathe`, `extrude`, `tube`) | Primitives are unit shapes scaled by `size`. `sphere` size is the **diameter**; `plane` is `[w, 1, d]` and lies in XZ. Unknown option keys are reported, not ignored. |
| `mesh.position.set(...)`, `rotation`, `scale` | Build time: `.position(x, y, z).rotate(x, y, z).scale(2)`. Runtime: `.runtime({ id, mutable: true })`, then `app.nodes.require(id).setPosition(x, y, z)`, `.setRotation`, `.setScale` | A node you move later needs `runtime({ id, mutable: true })`. Handles have `set*`, not `.position.x`. Vectors are tuples, not `Vector3`. |
| `Group` / `Object3D` hierarchy, bones as groups | `group("arm", [children], { position }).runtime({ id, mutable: true })` | Children use local transforms; a group's origin is its pivot. Since 5.7.0 model and primitive handles inside a group are parent-local too (5.6 took world coordinates: convert such code or make the node top-level); world reads use `getWorldPosition()`. |
| `BufferGeometry` + `setAttribute` + `setIndex` | `geometry.custom(geometry.define({ positions, normals, uvs, colors, indices, bounds }), { name, material })` | Typed arrays in; `bounds` required; `colors` are per-vertex RGBA. `geometry.dynamic` for geometry you rewrite. |
| `MeshStandardMaterial` | `material.pbr({ color, roughness, metallic, emissive, opacity })` | Also `physical` (clearcoat), `emissive`, `toon`, `matcap`. Colour is a CSS string. |
| `ShaderMaterial` | `material.custom({ glsl: { vertex, fragment }, uniforms: { t: { type: "f32", value: 0 } } })`; `handle.setUniform("t", v)` | GLSL 3.00 (`in`/`out`, write `outColor`). Prelude names: `position`, `normal`, `uv`, `modelViewProjectionMatrix`, `modelMatrix`, `cameraPosition`, `uTime` (wall-clock seconds; advances only while the app redraws every frame: give the node `.runtime({ id, mutable: true })` or register `app.onFrame(...)`, else a static scene draws once and `uTime` looks frozen). Node/TSL: `material.node`. |
| `DirectionalLight` + `castShadow` | `lights.directional({ position, target, intensity, shadow: true })` | `shadow: true` on the light; meshes take `castShadow` / `receiveShadow`. Also `point`, `spot`, `hemisphere`, `ambient`, `rect`. |
| `scene.environment = pmrem` | `environments.neutral({ intensity, background: false })` (also `studio`, `outdoor`, `hdri`, `preset`) | Metals render dark without an environment. `looks.preset(id)` bundles environment, key light, fog and grade. |
| `scene.background = sky shader`, `Sky` | `sky.preetham({ sun: { elevationDeg, azimuthDeg } })`, `sky.gradient`, `sky.dayNight` | Move the sun live with `app.atmosphere.setSky({ sun })`. |
| `scene.fog = new FogExp2` | `effects.fog({ color, density })` | A scene node, not a property. |
| `InstancedMesh` + `setMatrixAt`/`setColorAt` | `instances.cone({ name, transforms: [{ position, rotation, scale }], colors: ["#...", ...], material })` | One draw call per node. Instance colour multiplies the material colour: use a `#ffffff` base material. |
| `AnimationMixer` + `clipAction().play()` | GLB: `app.nodes.require(id).play("Idle", { loop: true, crossFade: 0.3 })`. Procedural: set joint handles in `onFrame` | Clips come from the file (`assets inspect --animation`). |
| `OrbitControls` | `interactions.orbit({ target: "node-name" })` + `camera.orbit({ position, target, fov })` | `target` is a node **name**, not a point. |
| `Raycaster.intersectObjects` | `raycast({ origin, direction })` or `interactions.pointer({ target })` + `bindPointerInteractions(app, listener)` | Returns hits against scene nodes, no object references. |
| `EffectComposer` + `UnrealBloomPass` | `effects.bloom({ intensity, threshold, radius })`, `effects.vignette`, `effects.colorGrade` | Passes are scene nodes; no composer. |
| `TextGeometry`, CSS2D labels | `text3D("Aura3D", { size, depth })`, `labels.billboard("score", { position })` | HUD belongs in the DOM. |
| `Points`, particle libraries | `effects.particles({ rate, lifetime: [a, b], speed, size, color, blend: "additive" })` | Built-in sprite atlas needs no art. |
| `geometry.dispose()`, `renderer.dispose()` | `app.dispose()` | One call disposes everything the app made. |
| `Vector3`, `Clock` | `[x, y, z]` tuples at option sites; `Clock` from `@aura3d/engine`; `Vector3` from `@aura3d/math/three` | Mutable three.js-shaped math lives only in `@aura3d/math/three`. |

Not here: `GLTFLoader` (use a typed asset, `model(assets.x)`; see `asset-workflow.md` (asset-workflow.md)), `renderer.toneMapping` (use the look preset's `output`), custom render targets and `EffectComposer` chains (no equivalent; check `docs/migration/from-threejs.md`).

Porting an existing file: `npx @aura3d/cli@latest migrate three "src/**/*.ts"` lists what maps, what is approximate and what to write by hand, as an annotated port worklist. Full mapping with verdicts: `docs/migration/from-threejs.md` (../migration/from-threejs.md).

Procedural scenes with no admitted model: docs/agents/recipes.md recipes 8 to 15 (humanoid with joints, heightfield terrain, instanced props kit, PBR product viewer, custom-shader water, sky and day/night, campfire particles, night street with bloom). Signatures: docs/agents/api-signatures.md.

Hello world: every scene gets a look first.

```ts
import { createAuraApp, looks, model, scene } from "@aura3d/engine";
import { assets } from "./aura-assets";

createAuraApp("#app", {
  scene: scene().add(looks.preset("product-studio")).add(model(assets.robot)),
  ...looks.appOptions("product-studio")
});
```

The quality floor — what the defaults give you, and the never list:

- A `looks.preset` supplies environment light (IBL), a shadow-casting key, fog,
  background and a post grade as one unit — never hand-wire
  `lights.ambient()` as the only fill, it flattens shading and kills IBL.
- Never a solid void background: the look's sky, biome or studio backdrop owns it.
- Never `pixelRatio`/`qualityProfile`/`safe-basic`/FXAA overrides or
  `replaceTextures: true` — `looks.appOptions(id)` carries the renderer contract.
- Never a hero subject made of primitives; `model(assets.x)` with a typed
  catalog asset.
- Never emissive cards or sprites faking reflections, puddles, splashes or glows —
  use the look's `post` grade and `effects.*`.
- Never CSS/DOM particles, overlays or labels standing in for rendered output;
  HUD lives in the DOM, the scene does not.
- Keep the key shadow at full strength with contact darkening at the subject's
  feet; fog or atmosphere carries depth to the horizon.

three.js → Aura3D mapping (corrected):

| three.js | Aura3D |
| --- | --- |
| `new THREE.Scene()` | `scene()` |
| `new THREE.Mesh(...)` + `new GLTFLoader()` | `model(assets.x)` (typed asset) |
| `new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(...)` | `camera.perspective(...)`, `camera.rigs.*` |
| `AmbientLight` | `lights.hemisphere(...)` or the look's environment fill |
| `DirectionalLight` key/fill | the look's `key`/`rim` slots |
| `scene.environment` + PMREM | `environments.preset|hdri`, `world.biome` |
| `toneMapping`/exposure | `output.preset` and the look's post grade |
| `setPixelRatio` | `quality: "auto"` via `looks.appOptions` |
| `castShadow = true` | `shadow: true` on the light/node |
| `EffectComposer` passes | `output.preset` + `effects.*` |
| `AnimationMixer` | `AnimationController` |
| `new OrbitControls(...)` | `interactions.orbit(...)` |

Effects, post-processing, atmospherics & VFX (`effects.*` in `@aura3d/engine`):
- Post-processing: `effects.bloom`, `effects.neonBloom`, `effects.cinematicBloom`, `effects.ambientOcclusion`, `effects.contactOcclusion`, `effects.contactShadows`, `effects.screenSpaceReflections`, `effects.depthOfField`, `effects.motionBlur`, `effects.colorGrade`, `effects.vignette`, `effects.filmGrain`, `effects.chromaticAberration`, `effects.antiAlias`, `effects.outline`
- Atmospherics & volumetrics: `effects.fog`, `effects.depthFog`, `effects.volumetricFog`, `effects.fogVolume`, `effects.lightCone`, `effects.auroraRibbon`, `atmosphere.setSky`, `atmosphere.setWetness`
- Particles, weather & trails: `effects.particles`, `effects.meshParticles`, `effects.rain`, `effects.snow`, `effects.flipbook`, `effects.trail`, `effects.beam`, `ResidentGPUParticleRenderer` (WebGPU compute)
- Game feel & genre kits: `game.feel` / `app.feel` (`hitStop`, `slowMo`, `damageFlash`, `speedLines`, `landingDust`, camera trauma), `game.platformer`, `game.racing`, `game.arcadeKart`, `game.grandPrixRoad`, `game.carSoccer`, `game.carSoccerPitch`, `game.racketSports`, `game.fallingBlocks`, `game.fighting`

Genre recipes (see `aura3d-art-direction/references/look-recipes.md`):

| Genre | Look | Camera + fov | Palette/accent | Atmosphere |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| platformer | `outdoor-day` | follow2d fov 50 | greens/sky/wood + gold | fog 0.0025 |
| racing | `golden-hour` | chase fov 60 | asphalt/orange/charcoal + amber | fog 30–180 m |
| fighting | `arena-fight` | fighting fov 45 | arena dark/rope/crowd + rim | haze cone |
| arena shooter | `space` | topDown fov 55 | space blue/graphite/teal + magenta | none |
| sports/table | `interior-industrial` | topDown fov 40 | turf/white/dark + ball | indoor haze |
| product | `product-studio` | orbit fov 35 | grey/white/metal + brand | none |
| character | `character-showcase` | orbit fov 40 | costume neutrals + rim | room haze |
| outdoor env | `overcast` | wide fov 55 | green/slate/fog blue + wildflower | fog 0.004 |
| interior | `interior-warm` | orbit fov 45 | wood/cream/spines + plant | dust shafts |
| night city | `night-city` | tele fov 35 | sodium/neon/asphalt + cyan | fog 15–90 m |
| space | `space` | orbit fov 60 | void blue/limb/stars + aurora | none |
| underwater | `underwater` | follow fov 50 | deep blue/teal/kelp + coral | scatter 0.03 |
| cinematic | `polar-night` | dolly fov 35 | aurora/snow/night + lantern | snow mist 0.006 |

The look-dev loop:

1. Pick the genre recipe row and 1–3 reference frames; write a 3-line look brief.
2. Build with the look preset and typed assets; no renderer overrides.
3. Capture `aura3d look capture --route / --shots opening,mid,action`.
4. Judge each frame against the quality-bar rubric; read `aura3d look lint`.
5. Fix the single highest-leverage thing; one change per round; repeat until
   every category reads 7+ or the loop exits flat.

Assets — resolve real objects from the catalog first. Do not invent asset paths,
URLs or ids — every model comes from a generated `assets.<key>`:

- `npx @aura3d/cli@latest assets search "<object>"` (natural descriptive phrase;
  it searches licence-tagged open public sources and a starter pack (there is no Aura3D-run search service to rely on);
  results are candidates to check, not guaranteed matches).
- `assets resolve "<object>" --name <name>` pulls the top auto-pullable match
  and types it as `assets.<name>` → `model(assets.<name>)`.
- Add local files with `assets add ./assets/model.glb --name model`, then read
  the generated `src/aura-assets.ts`.
- Playable characters: `assets resolve "animated humanoid fighting character"
  --profile fighting-character` keeps provenance in `aura.assets.json`.
- Other model formats: `assets convert in.fbx --out out.glb` turns FBX, OBJ,
  DAE, USD, PLY, STL, 3MF, VOX or BVH into a verified GLB (partial parity;
  every loss is reported as a diagnostic).
- Lifelike custom models: `assets generate "<subject>" --name <key> --kind
  character|creature|vehicle|object [--rig --animations idle,walk,run]
  --dry-run` prints the fal.ai cost (reference still $0.17, skipped with
  `--image`; Idol mesh $0.20, $0.25 rigged); the paid run refits the skin,
  optimises, faces +Z, grounds, scales, slims normal maps (JPEG) and admits a
  `candidate` with `<key>.idol.json` provenance. `assets normalize` (facing,
  size, grounding), `assets slim` (JPEG normal maps) and `assets preview`
  (CPU base-colour preview sheet, not a render) work on any GLB;
  `assets thumbnail` writes manifest PNG thumbnails the same way.
- Generated PBR maps are not trustworthy as delivered (lessons-learned A11,
  A12). A Hunyuan 3D car arrived as one material with metalness median 0.77,
  roughness 0.17 and a JPEG normal map tilting 7 degrees on panels that should
  be smooth: blotchy sheen, wavy reflections, dented paint. After generating,
  inspect metalness, roughness and normal-tilt statistics; make painted bodies
  dielectric (metalness about 0) with a clearcoat; split body, glass, chrome
  and tyres into separate materials; keep normal maps lossless PNG; lower
  `normalScale` on reconstructed meshes; judge glossy surfaces on a real GPU.
  Never run `assets slim` on glossy or mirror models (it writes JPEG normal
  maps); rebuild a glossy generated hero from the raw download with
  `assets optimize` and `assets normalize`, which do not re-encode normal maps
  (a normal map the generator delivered as JPEG stays damaged: lower
  `normalScale` or drop it on smooth surfaces).
- Motion: `animation import <file.bvh|.fbx|.glb|motion.json> --onto rig.glb
  --out hero.glb` retargets clips onto a humanoid rig as real glTF clips and
  fails on limb flips, a frozen T-pose or skin damage (known defects go in
  `aura.skin-allow.json`; `--strict` fails on any unlisted skin error).
  `animation generate "<motion>" --onto rig.glb --out hero.glb` makes clips
  from text with fal.ai HY-Motion ($0.08 per clip) and imports them.
- fal.ai key lookup: `FAL_KEY`, then `--key-file`, then
  `~/.config/aura3d/fal.env`, then `~/.config/auraone/fal.env`; never printed.
  `--dry-run` makes no paid call; every submit is ledgered in
  `.aura3d/fal/ledger.jsonl` and a rerun resumes pending requests instead of
  paying twice.
- Every command, flag and exit code: `aura3d help --json`, or
  `docs/api/cli-reference.md` (generated from it).

Scaffold:

```bash
npx create-aura3d@latest my-scene --template product-viewer
npx create-aura3d@latest my-fighter --template fighting-game
cd my-scene && npm run dev
```

Mandatory 3D game & scene anti-failure guardrails:

1. High-craft 3D models — curated/rigged GLBs or multi-part procedural `@aura3d/engine` sculpting (never 1-box programmer art and never default to melted-clay blobs) & prop normalization (`targetMaxDimension` vs `targetHeight`):
   - Never assemble characters, athletes, enemies, vehicles, aircraft, trees, or architectural landmarks out of 1 to 3 raw unchamfered `primitives.box`, `primitives.sphere`, or `primitives.cone` placeholders ("no stick-figure humans, 1-box cars, or single-cone trees").
   - When a clean, crisp, properly UV'd or rigged skeletal 3D GLB exists in `src/aura-assets.ts` or open CC0/CC-BY sources, mount it via `model(assets.<name>, { targetMaxDimension, role })` (use `targetHeight` only for upright humanoids and `targetMaxDimension` for horizontal vehicles, rackets, paddles, weapons, barriers, and wide props so aspect ratios and silhouettes never stretch vertically).
   - When no clean GLB exists (or when existing candidates are muddy single-texture clay blobs), sculpt a bespoke multi-part, multi-material procedural assembly directly in `@aura3d/engine` using `primitives.extrude` (beveled 2D profiles), `primitives.lathe` (turned domes, wheels, barrels, hulls, foliage), `primitives.tube` (spline arches, roll-cages, branches, rigging), `primitives.roundedBox` (chamfered plates and timbers), `primitives.polyhedron`, and `geometry.define` + `geometry.applyMatrix4` + `geometry.merge` + `geometry.multiMaterial` + `instances.custom` split across 3 to 8 distinct physical materials (`material.carPaint`, `material.lacquer`, `material.brushedMetal`, `material.ceramic`, `material.studioGlass`, `material.fabric`, `material.physical`).
   - Drive rigged humanoid and creature GLBs (`skins > 0`) via `handle.setAnimation({ clip, loop: true, speed })` (or `AnimationController`) synchronized to locomotion (`idle`, `walk`, `run`, `attack`, `swing`), and articulate multi-part procedural characters/machines (`group` joints, rotors, wings, suspension, turrets) every frame under the key light and shadow instead of sliding rigid statues across the floor.
2. Boot sequence gate (`app.ready().then(...)`, never a module top-level `await`) & default manual control (`autopilot = false` on Frame 1):
   - Gate Frame 1 on `app.ready().then(...)` (a module top-level `await app.ready()` deadlocks a production build: black page) before fading out `#boot-gate` (`opacity: 0; pointer-events: none` then remove) and starting the gameplay simulation loop so lighting, shadow, and GLB silhouettes never pop in mid-frame.
   - Default `autopilot` / AI demo mode to `false` (immediate manual control on Frame 1 once `#boot-gate` clears); every game supports `?autoplay=1`: read the flag with `readAutoplayFlag(location.search)` (accepts `autoplay`, `autopilot`, `demo`) and run the bot and the results-hold-then-restart loop on `createAutoplayHarness` from `@aura3d/engine/game` (never a hand-written flag reader or restart timer); the HUD `Auto` toggle flips `harness.enabled`, and manual input (keyboard, pointer, touch, gamepad) takes control back.
   - Keep mode, stage, camera, `Auto`, and roster selectors in a compact, non-blocking top HUD bar that preserves camera framing, and always call `button.blur()` after button clicks so `Space` or `Enter` gameplay keys never re-trigger focused HUD buttons.
3. Always optimize heavy 3D GLBs before admission (`aura3d assets optimize --file in.glb --out out.glb --role <role>`):
   - Raw exports often contain `200,000–1,750,000` vertices and `20–65 MB` of uncompressed 4K PNG textures, which stall main-thread glTF parsing and exhaust GPU memory when multiple models load in one scene.
   - Role budgets: prop 6,000, background 15,000, character 30,000, hero or vehicle 40,000 vertices; textures capped at 1024 to 2048 px; 16-bit indices; keep a game's assets near 25 MB. Admit the optimised file with `assets add` into the game's own project, never from the repo root while other work is open.
4. Always use canonical typed asset manifest refs (`hash` required):
   - The production glTF bridge requires `createAssetProvenance(node.asset).source === "typed-aura-assets-manifest"`, which requires a valid 64-character `sha256-...` `hash` and `public/aura-assets/...` provenance from `aura.assets.json` / `src/aura-assets.ts` so the rendered look and silhouette load cleanly.
   - Never omit `hash` in custom `defineAssets(...)` declarations and never place unhashed duplicate GLBs in route-local `apps/<route>/public/aura-assets/` that collide with root `public/aura-assets/`.
5. Mutate node handles instead of calling `app.setScene()` on every restart:
   - Do not call `app.setScene()` when restarting a round, hole, or bout on the same stage/world; tearing down and remounting the scene disposes live GPU resources, breaks lighting and postprocess continuity, and aborts in-flight GLB loads. Track a scene signature (`stageId` / `worldId`) and reset positions, visibility, and animations through runtime node handles (`app.nodes.require(...)`).
6. Prevent fog whitewash, overexposure, and instanced emissive blowout:
   - If a fast route whitewashes, pass `{ fogDensityScale: 0, exposureEv: -0.1 }` to `looks.preset(...)` for that route. Never pin post-processing, the compiler or fog off for every player with a `qualityRebuild.flags` list: it hides bugs and flattens the look. Install `installSafetyNet` from `@aura3d/debug` so a machine that renders black steps down one rung on its own and `?diag=1` shows the GPU, limits and shader failures.
   - Never set `emissive: "#ffffff"` with high `emissiveIntensity` on an instanced pool material (`instances.box` / `primitives.box({ instances })`): per-instance `instanceColors` multiply `u_baseColor`, not `u_emissiveColor`.
7. Ground `model()` feet on platform top surfaces (`y + sy / 2`) & wind custom meshes CCW:
   - `model(asset, { targetHeight })` normalizes the GLB with `minY = 0` (feet at `position[1]`), whereas `primitives.box` and `primitives.cylinder` (`instances.box` / `instances.cylinder`) are centered on `[-0.5..+0.5]` so a platform at `(y, sy)` has its top surface at `y + sy / 2`. Always place grounded characters and vehicles at `platform.y + platform.sy / 2` so they never sink into logs, pads, or road lanes. Wind custom `geometry.custom` triangles CCW when viewed from `+Y`.
8. Enforce full-viewport `100vw × 100vh` canvas, deep ground apron, and pushbox separation:
   - Size `html, body, #app, canvas` to `100vw × 100vh` (`position: fixed; inset: 0; overflow: hidden`) and extend the 3D ground/stage apron deep enough in `+Z`/`-Z` under the camera frustum so the bottom third of the viewport never shows a black clear-color void. Disable `collision: true` on `camera.rigs.shoulder` when the target character has attached child runtime nodes, and enforce `>= 1.4m` fighter pushbox separation (`|x| >= 1.8m` at spawn).


Kits (build the shell from these, do not hand-roll it):

- `@aura3d/engine/game`: `createGame` (lifecycle, pause, results, DOM HUD, touch, juice, game sound); the root `createGame` throws a `CREATE_GAME_ROOT_UNAVAILABLE_V1` migration error.
- `@aura3d/engine`: `createFixedStepLoop`, `installQaHooks` (`window.__AURA_<NAME>__`), `readQaParams`, `createCountedRng` for deterministic replay and automated checks; 5.5.5 QA telemetry: `installQaTelemetryHooks` (adds `checkState`, `measureFrame`, `telemetry`, `resetTelemetry` hooks), `createQaRunMonitor` (step vs frame timing, input-aware stuck detection), `findNonFinitePaths(state)` (`NaN`/`Infinity` paths), `hashQaPixels(pixels)`, `installVirtualGamepads()` (4 scripted `"standard"` pads, replay tokens such as `"Pad1A"`), `createQaOfflineAudio()` + `analyzeQaAudioSamples(channels, sampleRate)` (clock-locked offline audio: peak/RMS dBFS, clipping, silence, onsets); `defineModelAssets` for hashed same-origin models with a `?models=0` procedural fallback; `scatterAlongPath`, `scatterInArea`, `splitScatterByDistance`, `mergeStatic` for draw-call budgets; `game.racketSports()` with `ballFlight`, `scoring`, `athleteRig`.
- `@aura3d/engine/audio`: `createCueBank`, `createStepSequencer`, `createToneLoop`, `createSampleSlices` on the single `AudioContextManager` (never `new AudioContext(`).
- `@aura3d/engine/devtools`: `createAuraTuneOverlay({ id, schema })` mounts a dev-only slider/enum panel (`Backquote` toggles it, `?tune` opens it); overrides persist with their authored baseline and drop when the source value changes; `diffBlock()` / `save()` export the changed constants to paste back into source.
- `@aura3d/debug`: `installSafetyNet` (`?diag=1`, quality switches `?post=0 ?shadow=0 ?env=0 ?sky=0 ?quality=low`, black-frame self-heal). `createBlackFrameWatch` is the watch it uses, exported for custom wiring; since 5.5.4 an all-`alpha === 0` probe (a WebGPU swapchain read outside its frame) counts as no sample, not a black frame.
- Runtime quality: `createAuraApp` runs `RuntimeQualityGovernor` (`@aura3d/rendering`, default on since 5.5.3), stepping across 5 rungs (render scale down to 0.67×) at a 16.67 ms budget without remounting. A fixed `renderer.quality` tier, `renderer.adaptive: false` or `?aura3d-adaptive=0` turns it off; `renderer.targetFrameRate` sets the budget. Details: `docs/api/quality-governor.md`.
- Wide gamut: `outputColorSpace: "display-p3"` in the renderer `output` options is a request; on the v2 post chain WebGPU negotiates Display-P3 or falls back to sRGB without throwing (5.5.4), and the renderer diagnostic report gives the active `outputColorSpace`. Claim P3 only from a real-device capture.
- Procedural sculpting: `@aura3d/engine/sculpt` (5.5.6) builds smooth organic meshes (`sculptOrganicSdfMesh`, `sculptStylizedHeadMesh`, `sculptSdfLimbChainMesh`, `sculptCurvedHairLockMesh`, `taubinSmoothMesh`, `assembleMultiMaterialNode`) for `geometry.define` / `geometry.multiMaterial`; bake once at load. New in 5.6.0: `sculptHairMassMesh`, `sminCubic`, `smaxCubic`. Details: `docs/api/sculpt.md`.
- Follow cameras: `computeCameraClearance(target, desired, obstacles, options?, out?)` from `@aura3d/engine` (5.5.6) pulls the camera in or lifts it over circle/box obstacles each frame. Details: `docs/api/motion-camera-clear.md`.
- Humanoid motion (5.6.0): `@aura3d/animation` exports `smplMotionToClip`, `skeletalMotionToFrames`, `mapHumanoid`, `createHumanoidDriver`, `detectHumanoidFacing` and `bakeHumanoidFramesToGltf`, the engine behind `aura3d animation import`. Since 5.7.0 play the clips with `createHumanoidAnimator` from `@aura3d/engine/animation` (cross-fades, mirrored clips, code poses; `humanoidLocomotionTime` drives clip time by distance so planted feet do not slide), never a per-game motion player. Details: `docs/api/humanoid-motion.md`.
- Game kits from the 30 live games (5.7.0, `@aura3d/engine/game`; use them, never hand-roll them): `readAutoplayFlag` + `createAutoplayHarness` (`?autoplay=1`, `docs/api/game-autoplay.md`); `createSnapshotInterpolator`, `mixNumber`, `mixVec3` (fixed-step render interpolation with a declared snap rule, `docs/api/motion-snapshot-interpolator.md`); `createImpactRig` (hit-stop, camera trauma, FOV kick on real frame time), `createProceduralSfx` (zero-asset cues), `ScreenFx`, `drainPopups`, `GameRng` (seeded counted RNG) (`docs/api/game-feel.md`); `createFlipbookAtlas` and `createGradingLut` (procedural flipbook VFX sheets and grading LUTs, `docs/api/game-vfx-sheets.md`). Recipe 18 in `docs/agents/recipes.md` wires them together.
- Look kits (5.7.0): `sky.gradient` stylised profile (`mid` bands, `horizonHeight`, `haze`, sun `glow` lobes and painted disc) is the painted game sky; write a custom dome only for clouds, stars or planets (`docs/api/sky-gradient.md`). Sun `shadow.softness` is the penumbra in shadow-map texels (`0` hard, `1` default, `2`-`4` soft; three.js `shadow.radius`) and `shadow.fit: { center, extent, depth }` pins the shadow map to a fixed box so texel size does not change with framing (`docs/api/shadow-softness.md`). A transparent canvas is `output: { alphaMode: "premultiplied", inputAlphaMode: "premultiplied" }` with no backdrop: it clears transparent, keeps the opaque frame's colours and keeps partial alpha on edges and `material.shadow` shadows (`docs/api/transparent-canvas.md`); never extract a matte from a coloured render.
- `material.custom` shaders: `#include <a3d_math>`, `<a3d_noise>`, `<a3d_sky>`, `<a3d_fog>`, `<a3d_triplanar>`, `<a3d_toon>`, `<a3d_shadow>` (sun shadows: `receiveShadow: true` on the spec, then multiply the lit term by `a3dSunShadowAuto(worldPos, normal)`), `<colorspace_decode>`; custom shaders write linear light, so use `a3dSrgbToLinear` with `toneMapping: "none"` for authored colours, and keep `pow`, `normalize`, `sqrt` and divides NaN-safe (Apple GPUs return NaN where software renderers do not).
- Production checks that CI missed: the bridge refuses http(s) or unhashed model URLs and then draws nothing; instanced and batched meshes honour texture maps; empty instance arrays are no-ops; real-GPU checks confirm what software-GL passes show. Docs: `docs/api/game-kit.md`, `qa-kit.md`, `quality-governor.md`, `safety-net.md`, `sculpt.md`, `humanoid-motion.md`, `audio-synth.md`, `model-loader.md`, `glsl-chunks.md`, `scatter-merge.md`, `cli-asset-tools.md`; pitfalls: `aura3d-core/references/pitfalls.md`.

Proof standard: use every feature freely; every claim ships with a judged capture.

- Name what a capability runs on: the `createAuraApp` safe API, `production-runtime`,
  `rendering` internals, the CLI asset pipeline, or a template scaffold; mark roadmap
  work as roadmap.
- Public examples show what the safe API renders through `@aura3d/engine`, backed by
  route health, typed provenance and a readable frame.

Release integrity:
- public examples use typed assets: no raw string asset IDs, raw GLB/glTF URLs, `unsafeModelUrl(...)`, `three` imports, or `GLTFLoader`;
- hero characters, vehicles, products, weapons, creatures and worlds are real models or labelled procedural recipes (abstract visualizations say so);
- particles in examples are Aura3D particles, not CSS/DOM;
- WebGPU, PBR, postprocess, skinned animation, morph and game-runtime claims come with matching browser evidence;
- showcase and README claims match detected capability, route-health evidence and screenshots.

Benchmark mode: if `aura3d look capture` is available, run the look-dev loop;
otherwise run finite commands (`npm install && npm run build`), then stop and
report the result as built but not yet look-checked.

| Scene Kit | API | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Material lab | `sceneKits.materialLab()` | root-proven (partial advanced coat extensions) |
